subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: When a Signal edit targets a message that has already entered session processing, should OpenClaw replace pending context without waking the agent, or also cancel and restart an active run?
rationale: The parser and identity repair are clear, but transcript mutation and active-run cancellation affect session semantics beyond Signal transport normalization and require an intentional product contract.

options.title: Bounded Signal supersession
options.body: Replace matching pending context, preserve edited metadata, and wake only on explicit mention while leaving active-run cancellation to the cross-channel issue.

options.title: Cancel and restart active runs
options.body: Treat an edit as superseding the active instruction and restart processing from corrected content, coupling this change to shared run-cancellation behavior.

options.title: Append an edit event
options.body: Keep both transcript entries but mark the later one as an edit, accepting additional context and possible model ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Bounded Signal supersession
recommendation.body: Replace matching pending context, preserve edited metadata, and wake only on explicit mention while leaving active-run cancellation to the cross-channel issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and existing issue review connect this person most directly to Signal inbound routing and the pending product-policy choice.
